title: Horizontal Logic — Executive Conviction
description: Consulting-grade executive-summary layout built on McKinsey horizontal-logic: action title above a hairline rule, three numbered evidence columns, and an 8pt italic source line at the footer. Unlike softer corporate templates, it enforces conclusion-first hierarchy with no decorative elements.
philosophy: This design exists to serve the consulting-firm conviction that a slide must lead with its conclusion, not bury it. It refuses label-style headers, decorative backgrounds, and any visual element that does not carry argumentative weight. The hairline rule beneath the action title is a deliberate cognitive separator — assertion above, proof below. It is built for rooms where credibility is earned through precision and every claim must be traceable to a source.
goodFor: Consulting deliverables structured around exactly three supporting data points
Executive briefings where the conclusion must precede the proof
Policy or research summaries requiring a cited footnote source line
avoidFor: Creative or brand pitches relying on visual storytelling and full-bleed imagery
Chart-heavy quarterly reviews needing large embedded graphs or tables
Audiences unfamiliar with management-consulting document conventions
Arguments with more than three supporting pillars or nested sub-bullets
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the cover of a high-stakes board memo — spare, institutional, and unapologetically text-forward. Compositional weight concentrates in the upper-left quadrant while the remaining canvas stays open and deliberately unhurried, signaling confidence rather than decoration. The hairline rule is the sole graphic device and must carry all visual drama by enforcing a hard cognitive boundary between the deck's central assertion and the framing context below. Avoid any illustrative element, tonal wash, or shape that does not serve the argumentative hierarchy.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with an 8% outer margin on all sides; the deck title is anchored left across cols 1–9, positioned in the upper-center third of the slide. A single hairline rule spans cols 1–9 immediately beneath the title, functioning as the assertion/proof separator even on the cover. Subtitle or deck descriptor sits below the rule in cols 1–7, with generous vertical breathing between the two text zones. Firm name and date attribution are set flush-right at the footer baseline; no folio number appears on the title slide.

examples.promptCore: The slide projects consulting-firm austerity — every element earns its presence by advancing the argument, nothing more. A commanding action title asserts the conclusion above the hairline rule; beneath it, three numbered columns deliver ordered, traceable proof with disciplined spacing that signals logical sequence rather than visual decoration. Avoid any softening gesture: no background texture, no illustrative fills, no secondary ornamental lines beyond the single cognitive separator. The mood is controlled boardroom authority — precision under scrutiny, where structure itself is the argument.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid with 6% outer margins; the action title occupies the full column span in a top band roughly 20% of slide height, separated from the proof zone by a single hairline rule spanning cols 1–12. Three equal-width numbered evidence columns sit in cols 1–4, 5–8, and 9–12 below the rule, each with a bold column header, body copy block, and internal vertical breathing room. An italic source citation anchors the bottom edge flush-left; a page number sits flush-right at the same baseline.
